title: What to Watch This Week: A Telugu God, a Malayalam Mastermind and Colin Farrell Walk Into Your Weekend
excerpt: The streamers stacked everything onto one Friday. From Drishyam 3 to Sonali Bendre’s comeback — here are the eight picks worth your subscription, and exactly where to find them.
body:
It's a brutal week to own a remote. The streamers didn't stagger their drops this Friday — they stacked them, all of them, on June 19, and now there's a Telugu god, a Malayalam patriarch, an Irish private eye and a Korean detective all fighting for the same Friday night. For the diaspora, this is the good kind of problem: almost everything worth watching is finally legal, subtitled and a click away, no dodgy stream required. Here's where to point yourself.

**The one you can't skip: Drishyam 3**

If you watch one thing this week, make it **Drishyam 3**, which landed on **Amazon Prime Video** on June 18 in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada. **Mohanlal** is back as Georgekutty, the family man who has spent two films out-thinking the entire Kerala police force, and **Jeethu Joseph** is back directing the cat-and-mouse he practically patented. The beauty of this franchise has always been that it doesn't need a single car chase to make your palms sweat — it's all ordinary men lying very, very carefully. For NRIs who've spent years tracking down grey-market links to the first two, having all four South Indian language versions drop on Prime the same day feels almost luxurious. Watch it before someone spoils the twist in the family WhatsApp group.

> The diaspora doesn't have to hunt for a theatre anymore — Georgekutty came home.

**The blockbuster victory lap: Dhurandhar 2**

**Dhurandhar 2: Raw and Undekha** hit **Netflix India** on June 19, and this is less a release than a coronation. **Ranveer Singh** and **Aditya Dhar**'s spy epic became the most-watched Indian film of its run, and the "Raw and Undekha" cut promises the bloodier, unseen footage that censors trimmed for theatres. If you missed it on the big screen — or simply want to relive Ranveer chewing scenery at full volume — this is your weekend. It's loud, it's nationalistic, it's exactly what it says on the tin. Pour something strong and lean in.

**The quiet stunner: Raakh**

Here's my sleeper pick. **Raakh**, on **Prime Video**, marks **Sonali Bendre**'s return to the screen after her very public battle with cancer, and by every early account she delivers the performance of her life opposite **Ali Fazal**. If you grew up on her '90s star wattage, watching her walk back into a frame older, steadier and fully in command is genuinely moving. This is the rare reason-to-subscribe-this-month title. Don't let the algorithm bury it under the louder drops.

**For the homesick funny bone: Save the Tigers 3**

Telugu's most beloved bunch of bickering married men return in **Save the Tigers Season 3** on **JioHotstar** (June 19), and this time the writers handed them a god — **Vennela Kishore** joins as Lord Indra, which is exactly the kind of unhinged escalation this marital comedy needed. It's breezy, it's regional, and it's the perfect antidote to a week of heavy thrillers. Pair it with **Athiradi**, Tovino Thomas's action-comedy on **SonyLIV** (also June 19, in five languages), if you want your laughs with a little more muscle.

**The international flex: Sugar Season 2**

For the Friday-night crowd who like their crime dressed in linen, **Sugar Season 2** returned to **Apple TV+** on June 19, with **Colin Farrell** back as the impossibly melancholic Los Angeles PI John Sugar. The first season's twist divided everyone, but Farrell's hangdog charisma never wavered. If you want pure noir mood — neon, jazz, a man who's too soft for his own job — this is your nightcap. Spy-drama loyalists should also flag **The Agency Season 2**, dropping on **Prime Video** on June 21.

**The wild card: Husbands In Action**

And because variety is the spice of a stacked weekend, **Husbands In Action** arrived on **Netflix** on June 19 — a Korean action-comedy about a narcotics detective forced to team up with his ex-wife's new husband to rescue her. It's chaotic, it's slapstick, and it's the kind of subtitle-friendly crowd-pleaser that travels effortlessly across living rooms from Edison to Wembley.

**The verdict**

If your weekend has room for exactly two, make it **Drishyam 3** for the craft and **Raakh** for the heart — one will keep you guessing, the other will catch you off guard. Everything else is gravy. The streamers have, for once, given the diaspora more than it can possibly finish. That's not a complaint. See you next Friday, when they'll almost certainly do it again.
